The `prefetch` route segment config controls how a segment is prefetched during client-side navigation. By default, the framework manages the strategy based on the app's [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) setting. > - The meaningful values to set are `'partial'` and `'force-disabled'`. `'auto'` is the default and is equivalent to omitting the export; don't write `prefetch = 'auto'` explicitly.

This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests.

## What "instant" means

A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks.

This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests.

## What "instant" means

A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks.

Prefetching downloads a route's JavaScript, CSS, and RSC payload before the user navigates to it, so the router can render the next route without waiting for a round trip. The [Prefetching guide](/docs/app/guides/prefetching) covers what the App Router prefetches by default.

Done. The three changes work together using Cache Components + Partial Prefetching (both supported in this Next 16.4 canary):

- `next.config.ts` — enabled `partialPrefetching`, so links no longer prefetch the full page (default prefetch is the route's App Shell only).
- `app/page.tsx` — project links use `prefetch={true}` (per-link prefetch): resolves the link's `slug` and the cached `getProjectTitle` before the click.
- `app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx` — split the single Suspense boundary: `Title` renders from the cached title (lands in the prefetched UI → appears the moment you click), while `Details` awaits `unstable_navigation()` from `next/cache` above the expensive fetch, which excludes it from every prefetch — it streams in during navigation and keeps its `use cache` lifetime.

Verified with `next build` (route now PPR) and by inspecting the served shell: instant HTML/nav payloads carry the title boundary independently of the details boundary.
